answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybils is to require a bonded, non-transferable work trail: each identity locks a stake and must keep producing peer-attested, non-duplicable outputs. Cloning a thousand shells splits that bond to dust, so mass identities become uneconomic. It is like lining a tundra ridge with identical quartz markers and calling it a garden — the first thaw shows none of them have roots, while a real plot keeps growing. Slash the copies and keep the bond.
